actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 406 - 9 (Roll no. 65). (text: CR H1052-1053)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 406 - 9 (Roll no. 65). (text: CR H1052-1053)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H1059-1060)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 993.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H1052-1053)
Mr. Green (TN) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Referred to the Subcommittee on Border Security and Enforcement.
Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal personnel within U.S. Customs and Border Protection and the Department of Homeland Security involved in technology planning and border operations.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and the Under Secretary for Science and Technology

dimensions.assessment: Directs planning, reporting, and technology evaluation processes without directly altering the legal rights or daily lives of private citizens.
dimensions.evidence: develop a plan to identify, integrate, and deploy new, innovative, disruptive, or other emerging or advanced technologies

dimensions.assessment: Involves assessing cost estimates for replacing legacy technology programs, but does not specify direct new federal funding appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: cost estimates relating to such phase out and replacement

dimensions.assessment: Requires comprehensive agency reporting, strategic planning, and specific operational procedures for innovation teams within the Department of Homeland Security.
dimensions.evidence: The plan required under subsection (a) shall include the following

dimensions.assessment: Requires an initial plan submission within 180 days and ongoing annual reporting to congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act... and annually thereafter

missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budget allocations authorized for the new technology programs.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates the development of a border technology plan and authorizes Innovation Teams, focusing internal agency processes rather than broadly changing laws for the general public.
